children: New Delhi, Sept. 21 -- Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited, Indian Oil Corporation Limited, Bharat Petroleum Corporation, Castrol India, and Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL) are among the top companies in the oil and energy value chain with attractive dividend yield.

Energy is emerging as a dominant theme for investors amid global headwinds like the West Asia crisis, inflation, etc. Higher dividend yield adds another layer of appeal as it will offer an additional source of income to investors. Here's the list of top 8 companies under this theme with highest dividend yield.

Gulf Oil Lubricants India share price was trading 0.98% lower at Rs.1058.10 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.5,243.47 crore at 2:18 pm on Monday, September 21. The stock has announced a total of Rs.51 per share dividend in FY26. With this, its dividend yield stood at 4.5%.

Indraprastha Gas Limited share price was trading 0.17% lower at Rs.149.15 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.20,881.02 crore at 2:22 pm. The company has announced close to Rs.4.75 per share dividend in last twelve months. Its dividend yield stood at 4.6% for FY26.

Sixth on the list is Castrol India. The company has a dividend yield of 4.7%. Its shares were trading 1.65% lower at Rs.193.80 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.19,169.19 crore at 2:27 pm. THe company has announced Rs.11.50 per share dividend in last twelve months.

Chennai Petroleum Corporation has a dividend yield of 4.5% for FY26. The company has announced Rs.62 per equity share dividend in the last one year. The company stock was trading 1.92% lower at Rs.1388.35 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.20,641.35 crore at 2:32 pm on Monday.

Bharat Petroleum Corporation share price was trading 1.63% higher at Rs.312.5 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.1,35,577.16 crore at 2:34 pm on Monday, September 21. The stock has a dividend yield of 5.5% for FY26.

Indian Oil Corporation share price was trading 0.40% higher at Rs.137.35 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.1,93,955.21 crore at 2:25 pm. It has a return on equity (ROE) of 16.33%. The stock has a dividend yield of 5.1% in FY26.

Government-backed, ONGC, is among the top companies with highest dividend yield. The O&G company has a dividend yield of 5.7%. The PSU stock was trading 1.2% higher at Rs.235.4 per share on BSE with an MCap of Rs.2,96,139.77 crore.

Hindustan Petroleum is on top of the list with 6.7% dividend yield for FY26. Hindustan Petroleum share price was trading 0.90% higher at Rs.357.7 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.76,112.21 crore at 2:40 pm.
